newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Foshan Lighting fined, suspended.
newsitem.headline: China's Foshan Lighting fined, suspended.

text.p: China's Foshan Lighting and Electrical Co Ltd was fined and suspended from trading on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on Friday for making illegal loans to a bank and a brokerage, a company statement said.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission confiscated Foshan's illegal profits of 39.67 million yuan and fined the company one million yuan, Foshan said in a statement to shareholders published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.

From May 1995 to November 1996, Foshan lent a total of 550 million yuan, including share proceeds of 260 million yuan, to a bank for annual interest rates of between 21.6 and 24.0 percent, the statement said.
Trading in the company's A and B shares was suspended on Friday, when the firm released the letter, the Shenzhen Stock Exchange said in a notice. Trading would resume on Monday, it said.
Foshan said it had also lent 80 million yuan to a brokerage firm at an annual interest rate of 25.2 percent in July 1996.
It did not identify the bank or the securities firm.
The company apologised to shareholders, saying these actions had violated rules governing lending and listed firms.
Foshan has recovered all the money lent to the bank and the brokerage, it said, adding the fine and cash seizure would not affect the company's 1996 profit distribution plan.
But the fine and confiscation of funds would be factored into 1997 earnings, the company said.
The issue of Foshan's 1996 dividend, a cash payment of 0.477 yuan per share, would be postponed to early August, it said.
China's securities authorities recently punished several brokerages and listed firms -- including Shenzhen's A share market leader Shenzhen Development Bank -- for stock-related irregularities.
